nodes.name: Ni substrate pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The Ni-based substrates were soaked in a 1 M HNO₃ mild acidic solution for 10 minutes before cell assembly or catalyst loading, followed by thorough washing with DI water.
nodes.source_text: The Ni-based substrates were soaked in a 1 M HNO₃ mild acidic solution for at 10 minutes before cell assembly or catalyst loading, followed by thorough washing with DI water.

nodes.name: Catalyst ink preparation
nodes.procedure: The catalyst ink was prepared by mixing catalysts with D2020 Nafion in a 1:3 (w:w) ratio of deionized (DI) water to 1-propanol (nPA), followed by sonication in an ice bath for over 30 minutes and subsequent aging (stirring at room temperature) for approximately one day.

nodes.name: Catalyst coating on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: The ink was then applied onto nickel foam via hand-spraying. After spray coating, the electrodes were dried at 60°C for at least 15 minutes, followed by additional drying at room temperature for over 24 hours to ensure proper adhesion and solvent evaporation.

nodes.description: Baseline AWE performance across multiple temperatures (40-80°C) with HFR correction
nodes.source_text: Electrochemical analysis comparing cathode and anode behavior reveals consistently greater overpotential for the cathode (HER)... charge transfer resistance (0.95 vs. 0.27 Ω cm²)... steeper Tafel slope (143 vs. 51 mV dec⁻¹)... HER overpotential exceeded the OER overpotential from as low as 0.12 A cm⁻², resulting in significant voltage loss... HER kinetic overpotential was reduced from 305.5 mV to 73.5 mV at 0.08 A cm⁻²... OER kinetic overpotential decreased from 322.7 mV to 243.3 mV at 2 A cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of nickel foam cathode shows white-line peak (1s→4p) shifts to higher energies with increased intensity after 24h at 2.0 V, indicating surface Ni oxidation and bonding with OH⁻ or H⁺ ligands.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis revealed shifts in the white-line peak (1s → 4p) to higher energies with increased intensity (Fig. 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS of nickel foam shows slight increase in Ni–Ni peak radial distance with preserved intensity, indicating bulk metallic Ni structure preserved but surface modifications occurred.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge Fourier transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) analysis showed a slight increase in the radial distance of the Ni–Ni peak, with no significant loss in intensity (Fig. 4c).

nodes.characterization_summary: WT analysis identifies Ni–M multi-scattering signal at ~3.5 Å in nickel foam, indicating incorporation of metal impurities (Fe, Al, Zn, Mn, Cu, Cr) from electrolyte.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wavelet transform (WT) analysis identified a multi-scattering Ni–M signal (~3.5 Å), aligned with the characteristic multiscattering region observed in the WT analysis of nickel foam

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L-edge XANES of Pt/C cathode after 24h voltage hold shows decreased Pt oxidation state with sustained white-line peak intensity, indicating stable ligand interactions with H⁺ or OH⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt L-edge XANES analysis indicated a decrease in the oxidation state of Pt, with sustained white-line peak intensity, suggesting stable ligand interactions with H⁺ or OH⁻ species (Fig. 4f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L-edge WT-EXAFS reveals multi-scattering signal near 4.5 Å corresponding to Pt–M–Pt bonds in Pt/C cathode, indicating interactions with migrated metal species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: WT analysis, which revealed a multi-scattering signal near 4.5 Å corresponding to Pt–M–Pt bonds, indicating potential interactions between Pt and migrated metal species

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES of NiFe anode shows decreased pre-edge and increased white-line peak intensity after 24h voltage hold, indicating transformation of NiFe alloy into Ni(Fe)OOH structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe K-edge XANES revealed a decreased pre-edge and increased white-line peak intensity, indicating the transformation of NiFe alloy into a Ni(Fe)OOH structure during this period (Fig. 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Fe–Fe bonding peak shift from 2.1 Å to 1.7 Å in NiFe anode, suggesting coordination with O-based species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FT-EXAFS analysis showed a shift in the Fe–Fe bonding peak from 2.1 Å to 1.7 Å, suggesting the coordination with O-based species such as O, OH, or OOH

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge WT-EXAFS confirms strong single-scattering signal at 1.7 Å for NiFe anode, verifying ligand interactions with oxygen species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: WT-EXAFS further confirmed these ligand interactions, with a strong single-scattering signal at 1.7 Å

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS reveals Pt/C cathode shows substantial charge transfer resistance reduction (significantly smaller semicircle in Nyquist plot) compared to bare nickel foam at 0.08 A cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS and DRT results at low current densities (0.08 A cm⁻²) revealed a substantial charge transfer gain, particularly at the cathode (Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows NiFe anode exhibits clear kinetic gain with reduced charge transfer resistance compared to bare nickel foam reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Pt/C (cathode) and NiFe (anode) combinations, the electrode with the catalyst exhibited a clear kinetic gain, whereas the opposing electrode (bare nickel foam) displayed potential and impedance characteristics similar to the reference case.
